subject: Polaris Systems: private listing — commercial exception & rev-share alignment
messages:
From: Alex Rodrigues <arodrigues@polaris-sys.com>
To: Chloe Martin <chloe_martin@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@polaris-sys.com
Date: 2028-09-04T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Private listing request: Polaris multi-year commitment

Chloe —

Great to meet the team yesterday. Polaris is ready to proceed via an AWS private listing, but procurement has two commercial asks that we need Redwood to consider for their board approval: 

- 30% off list for the first 12 months (applied to yearly committed spend)
- Rev-share to Polaris of 18% on marketplace revenue (they expect higher because of co-sell and lead generation)
- 36-month term; willing to prepay the first year

I've attached the SOW and our forecast for context. They need a yes/no on the commercial exception by 9/10 to align with our internal approval cycle.

Are these things we can approve at Deal Desk, or should we escalate to execs? If escalation is required, who in your team should I expect to see looped in?

Appreciate a quick read — Alex

--
Alex Rodrigues
Director, Strategic Accounts
Polaris Systems
arodrigues@polaris-sys.com

Attachments: Polaris_SOW_v2.pdf, Polaris_Monthly_Forecast.xlsx

From: Chloe Martin <chloe_martin@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Rodrigues <arodrigues@polaris-sys.com>
Cc: procurement@polaris-sys.com, ben_carter@redwood.ai
Date: 2028-09-04T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Private listing request: Polaris multi-year commitment

Alex — thanks for the details and the fast turnaround. I can lead the marketplace private listing flow; a few quick notes before we lock anything: 

- Rev-share >15% is outside standard marketplace carveouts and requires exec approval + finance sign-off.
- 30% discount is non-standard but not impossible if we get a solid ARR commitment and marketing co-fund.
- We need the final annual committed spend number and confirmation of who will accept AWS invoicing terms (Polaris or a reseller).

I am looping in Ben (Marketplace Sales Ops) and Lauren (Finance) to get preliminary guidance; if Ben/Finance push back, I will escalate to Marissa for exec approval.

Can you confirm the annual commit ($) and whether Polaris can accept standard Net30 with a procurement P.O.? That will materially affect the ask.

Best,
Chloe Martin
Principal Account Executive\Redwood Inference\chloe_martin@redwood.ai

On 2028-09-04 09:12, Alex Rodrigues wrote:
> Chloe —
>
> Great to meet the team yesterday. Polaris is ready to proceed via an AWS private listing...

From: Chloe Martin <chloe_martin@redwood.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-09-04T11:02:00-07:00
Subject: FW: Polaris commercial exception request — need deal desk recommendation

Team — forwarding Polaris' ask (below). TL;DR: they want 30% off year 1 + 18% rev-share. Procurement needs a commit decision by 9/10.

Quick context and proposed options for approval path:
- Polaris is strategic; mid-market with enterprise GTM through AWS. First-year committed ARR estimate from their forecast: $600k (see attached).
- Ask is outside Deal Desk guardrails due to rev-share >15% and discount depth.

Options I see: 
A) Counter with commercial compromise we can sign off at Deal Desk: 25% discount + 15% rev-share, annual prepay for Y1.
B) Accept 30% discount + 18% rev-share but require: $600k committed ARR (12-month), co-marketing fund $50k, and CS onboarding milestones with clawback (30/60/90 day usage gates) — needs Marissa approval.
C) Deny the rev-share ask and offer standard marketplace split; keep discount at 20% and push for enterprise channel incentives instead.

Asks: Ben — can you validate operational impact / billing path for option B (AWS listing with higher vendor share)? Lauren — are those financial terms (28–30% discount + 18% rev-share) tolerable if we secure the $600k ARR and co-marketing? Vivek — thoughts on strategic value / willingness to escalate to Marissa for exec approval?

I put Marissa on the thread since this will likely need exec sign-off if we pursue Option B. Please reply with your recommendation and any redlines by EOD 9/05 so I can respond to Polaris before their board window.

Thanks — Chloe

Attachments: Polaris_SOW_v2.pdf, Polaris_Monthly_Forecast.xlsx

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Chloe Martin <chloe_martin@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-09-05T14:20:00-07:00
Subject: Re: FW: Polaris commercial exception request — need deal desk recommendation

Chloe / team — quick read: I can support escalation to Option B (exec approval route) provided we lock two operational protections:

1) Minimum committed ARR of $600k for year one (annual prepay or automated PO).
2) Marketing co-fund of $50k from Polaris to offset customer acquisition; we require a 6-month co-marketing plan and milestone payments.
3) Clawback linked to usage: 30/60/90 day usage gates with partial refund triggers if deployment doesn't meet agreed thresholds.

If leadership prefers to keep rev-share <=15% and still move fast, I recommend countering with 28% discount + 16% rev-share (middle ground) and require the $600k commit + onboarding deliverables. That will keep finance happier and reduce marketplace margin impact.

Operationally, AWS private listing supports custom rev-share splits via their billing flow but it will add ~2 weeks to setup if we need special invoicing or POs.

Ben
Marketplace Sales Ops
ben_carter@redwood.ai

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Chloe Martin <chloe_martin@redwood.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>, legal@redwood.ai, finance@redwood.ai
Date: 2028-09-06T16:33:00-07:00
Subject: Re: FW: Polaris commercial exception request — need deal desk recommendation

Chloe — I've reviewed the thread and Ben's recommendations. Approved to move forward with a one-time commercial exception under these conditions: 

- Final terms to offer Polaris: 28% discount for Y1, 16% rev-share to Polaris on marketplace revenue.
- Minimum committed ARR: $600,000 for the first 12 months, evidenced by signed PO or prepay.
- Co-marketing commitment: $50,000 (plan required before listing goes live).
- CS onboarding milestones & clawbacks must be in the SOW (30/60/90 usage gates).
- Legal to include standard indemnities, data handling addendum, and ensure AWS billing/PO path is acceptable. Finance to confirm cashflow impact and that Net30 remains the default. Any Net60 request must be approved separately by Finance.

Chloe, you have the green light to present the compromise to Polaris and request a signed PO by 9/14. If Polaris accepts, loop Legal and Finance for redlines and coordinate AWS Marketplace provisioning with Ben. Keep me posted on any deviations.

Approved — Marissa Cole
SVP, Commercial
marissa_cole@redwood.ai
